newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI FINANCE FIRMS SEEN TAKING 6-8 MONTHS TO REFORM.
newsitem.headline: THAI FINANCE FIRMS SEEN TAKING 6-8 MONTHS TO REFORM.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Wednesday 58 cash-strapped finance companies suspended by the government since late June would take six to eight months to reform through mergers among themselves or with stronger firms.

Thanong told a radio station the suspended firms and their prospective new partners would need to review the quality of assets of the suspended companies and especially loans extended to the ailing property sector.

Thanong, returning from Tokyo, where he obtained a $16 billion multilateral pledge of loans to help Thailand ride out its financial problems, said: "Everyone (in the finance sector) must acknowledge that their business faces problems of asset quality."
"Substandard assets, especially those kept in the property sector, must be set aside, otherwise the non-performing loans would weaken future merged companies," he said.
The Bank of Thailand has said 42 of the 58 suspended firms would stop doing normal finance business for at least three months while auditors were appointed to review their books.
The suspended firms are saddled with high non-performing loans extended to the collapsed property sector.
Thanong said: "Everyone needs to be patient and accept the fact that business can produce either profits or losses."
